To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the most effective way of reducing emissions from road transport, while meeting air quality objectives, is to reduce car size and increase fuel efficiency, and that the introduction of biofuels, hydrogen and electric vehicles is unlikely to have any significant impact on air quality, unless these vehicles are used in a very limited way.
• A 15% reduction in average new car engine sizes would have the largest impact on air quality, with a 20% reduction in NOx emissions and a 15% reduction of particulate matter.
• The most cost-effective way to achieve the required reductions is to focus upon the most polluting vehicles.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the implications of the range of options available for the reduction of emissions from the road transport sector.

the implications of alternative policy measures for the road transport sector in the UK, with the aim of reducing local, national and transboundary emissions of air pollutants and greenhouse gases, and of identifying potential co-benefits.
identifying strategies that will be effective in achieving multiple environmental objectives and which are compatible with other policy developments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is a wide range of options, but that no one option will meet all the criteria, and the best choice depends upon the context.

there are no easy answers to the problem of reducing road transport emissions and that the most appropriate strategy for any country will depend upon the relative priorities of the different policy objectives.

the best way forward is a mix of strategies that include a range of behavioural changes, a reduction in the size of the vehicle fleet, and the introduction, in particular, of low carbon vehicles into the mix of vehicles.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the potential benefits from the introduction of electric vehicles are considerable in terms of both local and national air quality, but that the benefits from other low carbon vehicles are less significant.
there is no one-size-fits-all solution for the abatement of road transport pollution.

the potential for significant reductions in air pollutants is still possible, but the scope for reductions is limited, and that the potential for reductions of CO2 emissions is more significant, but that this will depend upon the choice of technology, and that the implications of these choices are significant for other sectors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, while the introduction of electric vehicles could be beneficial to air quality, it would have little impact on climate change.
, in addition to end-of-pipe abatement, behavioural and technological changes are needed to achieve the environmental objectives.
, in order to meet air quality objectives, it is important to consider a mix of strategies that can include both behavioural change and technological change.
